regression_guard: gci_C rebuilt through the new te-opening code path: 603,592 cells, max node difference 0.000e+00 m against the mesh on disk. Bit-identical.
gating: all eight solves ACCEPTED, residuals 6.36-7.65 orders

ladder_A_n_base.what: n_base 5 -> 7 -> 9, i.e. 4 -> 6 -> 8 cells ACROSS the blunt face. Everything else held. A pure mesh test: the base geometry is unchanged at 4.336 mm, 0.500 % of chord.
ladder_A_n_base.verdict: CONVERGES. Differences shrink -8.510 -> -5.033 at a0 and -8.621 -> -5.053 at a4, condition ok on both. So the base face is GRID-LIMITED, not model-limited: more cells across it do fix it.
ladder_A_n_base.but: p = 0.52 on CDp and CD at both incidences. That is below first order -- convergence is SLOW, and the extrapolation sits 31 counts below the finest level tried. Grid-limited does not mean cheaply fixable.
ladder_A_n_base.efficiency: nb9 recovers 63 % (a0) and 66 % (a4) of the whole gci_C -> gci_M CDp shift for +5.6 % cells, against gci_M's +94 %. About twelve times more drag-error removed per cell added.

the_agreement_worth_noting.claim: Two orthogonal refinement directions extrapolate to the same pressure drag.
the_agreement_worth_noting.caveat: Both are Richardson extrapolations at low observed order (1.83 chordwise, 0.52 n_base), and Richardson is fragile there. Agreement between two independent directions is nevertheless a real convergence indicator and is better evidence for a limit near CDp 66 at alpha 0 than either estimate alone.

ladder_B_opening_law.what: The opening law scaled: base 0.500 % -> 0.300 % -> 0.200 % of chord, at fixed n_base and every count held. THIS IS A GEOMETRY CHANGE -- the opening is made by adding thickness to the loft, so these are different wings.
ladder_B_opening_law.cells: 603,592 on all three -- the mesh does not change size, only the wing does
ladder_B_opening_law.verdict: Shrinking the base from 0.500 % to 0.200 % of chord removes 15.0 counts of pressure drag at a0 and 14.8 at a4, while viscous drag moves 0.09 counts. C_L moves 28 counts, confirming these really are different wings rather than the same wing meshed better.
ladder_B_opening_law.reading: About 15 of the 22.4 counts of base drag are a consequence of choosing 0.500 % rather than the 0.2 % that is ordinary practice. That choice was never justified in this repository.

combined_conclusion: The base is grid-limited, so it CAN be fixed with cells -- but at p = 0.52 it is expensive to fix, and it is 0.5 % of chord when 0.2 % is normal. The cheapest route to a smaller, better-converged base term is to do BOTH: raise n_base, which is nearly free at +2.8 % cells per step, and shrink the opening, which costs nothing at all. Shrinking it also shrinks the poorly-converging term itself.
still_open: Whether raising n_base removes the DIVERGENCE seen under wall-normal refinement (gci_C_normal moved base drag +23.1 counts). Ladder A did not test that -- it held eta fixed. If the divergence survives a well-resolved base face, the near-wake reading stands; if it does not, the divergence was an under-resolved base face all along.
